Title: Marks that lag, and a gap that shouldn't comfort anyone

Rating: underweight

Grimshaw Partners, 2028-03-15. The data panel offers a study in reassurance that dissolves under scrutiny. A reported drawdown of +0.0% against a reported-vs-public gap of -0.8% is not evidence of stability; it is evidence of a marking convention that has not yet caught up to the public market's own repricing.¹ Private credit valuations move at the speed of their committees, not their collateral. When the gap between reported and public marks sits persistently negative, the honest reading is that private books are behind, not that they are insulated.

The rival house — Calder & Root — reads policy support as resolution: rates steady at 4.50%, spreads at a seemingly tame 320bps, equities extending gains, issuance windows reopening. We read the same tape as delay. A 320bps spread is not compression so much as complacency priced into a market where new issuance is reopening precisely because sponsors need refinancing runway before conditions tighten again. The one_year_return of +15.0% against a ytd_return of +6.0% suggests deceleration already underway, even as headline sentiment (equities extending gains) papers over it.

CPI at 2.4% gives policymakers room to hold rather than cut, which removes the tailwind the rival's thesis depends on. Structurally, fragilities compound quietly in private credit — covenant loosening, extend-and-pretend restructurings, valuation lag — long before they show up in a drawdown figure. The absence of drawdown today is not proof of absence of stress; it is proof that stress has not yet been marked.

Risk to this view: if issuance windows reopening genuinely reflect broad-based balance-sheet repair rather than refinancing necessity, the reported-vs-public gap could close constructively, vindicating the rival's "stay the course" read rather than ours.

¹ A chart of reported versus public marks, plotted monthly, would show two lines converging late and reluctantly — the private line always arriving after the public one has already moved.
